title: Choose Bevel normal correction from surface type and cage distribution
problem: A rim Bevel bends planar-cap and curved-side normals, but a flat-panel Weighted Normal rule can worsen an uneven curved skin instead of repairing it.
preconditions: the bevel represents a real physical rim or manufactured edge radius
the intended curved surface and planar regions are identified separately
the base cage's angular spacing and analytic or reference-defined curvature can be inspected
modifier evaluation remains live so alternate policies can be compared without destroying the cage
required_observations: unbeveled smooth curved-side baseline under the same cage distribution
curved-region normal or highlight error after Bevel
angular spacing or face-area distribution around the curved skin
modifier order, Harden Normals flag, Face Strength mode, and Weighted Normal Face Influence
action_policy: Do not transfer a flat-panel Weighted Normal success to a curved skin without a separate curved-region check.
Compare the beveled result with an unbeveled semantic baseline so Bevel-induced error is separated from error already encoded by the cage.
Use Bevel Harden Normals when the goal is to preserve surrounding face normals through a local physical rim; verify that it restores rather than invents the curved-side baseline.
Use Bevel Face Strength followed by Weighted Normal only when its weighting modes suit the actual face-area and angle distribution; inspect curved regions independently from planar panels.
If the restored baseline is still wrong, repair radial spacing, density, or surface topology. Do not add another normal modifier to conceal geometric distribution error.
Treat equal segment count as insufficient evidence: angular distribution controls radial normal quality and highlight rhythm.
expected_effects: planar cap normals stay flat while the physical bevel carries the highlight transition
Harden Normals returns curved-side shading to the cage's unbeveled baseline
uniform 12-16 sided radial cages at the tested scale remain near their analytic side-normal target
uneven spacing remains visible as a topology problem rather than being mislabeled a Bevel failure
failure_predicates: Weighted Normal reduces planar error but increases curved-side analytic or visual error
the unbeveled baseline already shows radial wobble or systematic normal error
technical manifoldness passes while MatCap or grazing highlights reveal uneven bands
normal-policy tuning is used to avoid correcting reference-critical silhouette or topology
recovery: disable the Weighted Normal candidate and restore the previous modifier checkpoint
enable Harden Normals on the scoped Bevel and compare against the unbeveled baseline
redistribute the existing radial vertices to appropriate angular spacing before increasing segment count
add density only where silhouette or highlight evidence still requires it, then repeat the matched comparison

sources.description: Harden Normals preserves surrounding faces; Bevel Face Strength is designed to feed a following Weighted Normal modifier.
Weighted Normal combines face normals using area, corner angle, or both, and can consume Face Strength.

experiments.description: Twelve saved fixtures compare unbeveled semantic baselines, plain smooth Bevel, Harden Normals, and Face Strength plus Weighted Normal across a uniform 12-sided cylinder, an equal-count uneven 12-sided cylinder, and a uniform 16-sided taper. A fresh process repeats all metrics and stack checks.
experiments.limitation: Low-sided controlled radial manufactured fixtures only; no SubD, arbitrary double curvature, unfamiliar prop, or human acceptance.

version_scope: Official current Manual behavior reproduced in Blender 5.2.0 LTS.
status_note: Experimentally tested across uniform cylinder, uneven equal-count cylinder, and taper. The result rejects blanket Weighted Normal use on curved skins and promotes topology-first diagnosis, but remains below runtime validation until used on a human-authorized reference asset.
